ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of Korea applies the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information as amended by Act No. 19498 and its Enforcement Decree; the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment; the Act on Prohibition of Financing for Public Intimidation; the Real-Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act; the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; and the supervisory regulations of the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU). There is no public beneficial ownership register in the Korean corporate registry. Beneficial owner identification files, covering all persons directly or indirectly owning 25 percent or more of shares, voting rights, or exercising de facto control, are maintained by financial institutions and reporting entities and are accessible only to KoFIU, supervisory authorities, and tax or justice authorities acting under statutory authority. Therefore the disclosure level for the Korean Yuhan Hoesa is Government_Only_Access.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Corporation Registration Extract from the Korean Commercial Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registry Office, National Court Administration, Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Origin: Republic of Korea. For a destination that is a Hague Apostille Convention member: certified registry extract, then notarization by a Korean notary public, then Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MOFA), with no consular legalization. For a destination that is not an Apostille Convention member: certified registry extract, then Korean notarization, then MOFA authentication or attestation, then consular legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the destination state in Seoul. The Hague Apostille route and the consular legalization route are mutually exclusive and are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean Business Registration Certificate, including tax clearance confirmation where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, district tax office of competent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention member destination: business registration certificate, then Korean notary, then MOFA Apostille, no consularization. Non-member destination: business registration certificate, then Korean notary, then MOFA authentication, then destination Embassy or Consulate in Korea for consular legalization. Only one route applies; apostille and consularization are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter) of Yuhan Hoesa, as adopted and duly certified
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators of Yuhan Hoesa and the Korean notary public certifying the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague member destination: notarized Articles of Association, then MOFA Apostille. Non-member destination: notarized Articles of Association, then MOFA authentication, then consular legalization by the destination state Consulate or Embassy in Seoul. The two authentication paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Incorporators Approving Incorporation, First Directors, and Authorized Signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Incorporators convened under the Korean Commercial Act, as attested by a Korean licensed attorney and notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: board resolution, Korean notarial attestation, MOFA Apostille, no consular legalization. For non-Apostille states: board resolution, Korean notarial attestation, MOFA authentication, destination consulate legalization in Korea. No chaining of Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for Incorporation Agent and Corporate Secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarial Office in Seoul, Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: executed power of attorney, Korean notary, MOFA Apostille. Non-Hague route: executed power of attorney, Korean notary, MOFA authentication, destination state Consulate or Embassy in Seoul for consular legalization. These routes are exclusive alternatives and are not applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Bank-Certified UBO and KYC Package
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed Korean commercial bank regulated under the Banking Act, after initial authority and customer due diligence verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille member destination: bank reference letter with bank seal and responsible compliance officer attestation, Korean notary, MOFA Apostille. Non-member destination: bank reference letter with bank seal and attestation, Korean notary, MOFA authentication, destination Embassy or Consulate in Seoul for consular legalization. The two routes are mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any engagement, all controlling persons, 25 percent or more UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories, intermediate parent entities, and beneficial owners by contract or trust must be screened against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, UK HMT sanctions list, and the Republic of Korea domestic measures under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Prohibition of Financing for Public Intimidation. Any PEP identification triggers enhanced due diligence, senior compliance committee approval, source of wealth review, adverse media analysis, and ongoing transaction monitoring under Article 4 of the Specific Financial Information Act. Matches on sanctions lists, shell indicators, or unexplained nominee structures require automatic refusal or a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU without tipping-off under domestic law. Screenings must be re-run before each disbursement and at every annual renewal.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea, operated by the National Court Administration at iros.go.kr, which provides the official duplicate-name search and commercial registration filing interface for Korean companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official statutory name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be a distinguishable Korean corporate name and must end with the Korean legal form suffix transliterated as Yuhan Hoesa. Foreign-language names are not accepted as the sole registered name. The registry applies a four-tier naming convention: first, a distinctive identifier; second, a business-descriptive or area-specific phrase; third, a Hangul phonetic transliteration of any non-Korean brand element; and fourth, the mandatory legal form suffix. If an English name is used, it must appear in parentheses after the registered Korean name and must be a faithful transliteration or directly corresponding name. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name of a company engaged in the same class of business under Articles 19 and 22 of the Korean Commercial

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-74 (Limited Liability Companies); Supreme Court Registration Rules; Local Tax Act registration duty provisions; Notary Officials Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Section of the District Court having jurisdiction over the principal office of the Yuhan Hoesa, with electronic lodgment available through the Supreme Court Registration Information Network (iROS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration of incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), filed under the Supreme Court Registration Rules and accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - the Korean Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the entire subscribed capital must be actually paid into a temporary escrowed bank account opened in the name of the company before the incorporation registration application is filed; the bank certificate of deposit must accompany the filing, and the funds cannot be withdrawn until the court registry completes the incorporation registration. Non-resident subscribers must remit funds through a licensed foreign exchange bank and report foreign direct investment under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A YUHAN HOESA UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA

At a meeting of the incorporators and the first board of directors of the Company, duly convened at the principal office on [DATE] at [TIME], with all directors present and waiving formal notice, the following agenda items were proposed, seconded, and unanimously passed as resolutions of the Company.

1. Capital Subscription and Contribution: RESOLVED, that the paid-in capital of the Company be fixed at Korean Won [AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] units of equal rights as specified in Article [X] of the Articles of Incorporation, and that the initial subscribers shown in the subscriber ledger have subscribed to all such units; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the full amount of the subscribed capital be deposited into a temporary capital subscription account in the name of the Company before the filing of the incorporation registration, and that the Representative Director be and hereby is directed to obtain a certificate of deposit from the bank and maintain the funds in the blocked account until the incorporation registration has been lawfully completed.

2. Banking and Accounts: RESOLVED, that [NAME OF REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR] and [NAME OF CFO], acting jointly or as otherwise designated, be and hereby are authorized to open, maintain, and operate corporate bank accounts, including merchant accounts for Stripe Billing and PayPal, to sign all account and KYC/AML undertakings, to execute checks and electronic fund transfer orders, and to approve payment instructions for the operation of the Multi-Channel Omni-Helpdesk and Conversational Bot Cloud business; and RESOLVED FURTHER, that any two authorized persons shall act as joint signatories for amounts exceeding Korean Won [THRESHOLD].

3. Registered Office: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and hereby is established at [COMPLETE ADDRESS], South Korea, which shall be the statutory seat of the Company and the venue for service of judicial and administrative documents; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director is authorized to sign the lease, obtain the landlord consent, and file the registered office details with the District Court Registry Office.

4. Statutory Officers: RESOLVED, that [NAME] be and hereby is appointed as the initial Director and Representative Director of the Company; [NAME] be and hereby is appointed as an initial Director; and [NAME] be and hereby is appointed as initial Statutory Auditor, unless exempt by the capital threshold under Article 409(4) of the Korean Commercial Act, each to hold office for a two-year term as set by the Articles of Incorporation and until a subsequent qualifying resolution of the members. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director and Director, jointly, be authorized to prepare, sign, and file the incorporation registration application, pay all registration fees, receive the commercial register certificate, issue certificates representing the ownership units, and carry out all corporate establishment procedures. All prior acts performed in furtherance of the incorporation and the subscription agreements are hereby ratified, affirmed, and adopted as acts of the Company.

This certification records the unanimous consent of all incorporators and directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Articles of Incorporation Preparation, and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Registration Information Network (iROS) for name availability; Korean notary public under the Notary Officials Act for notarization.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name clearance search on the iROS electronic registration system to confirm that the proposed Korean trade name is not identical or deceptively similar to an already-registered company in the same nationwide registry. If the name is available, prepare Korean-language Articles of Incorporation stipulating the corporate purpose, number and par value of units, paid-in capital, registered office, initial officers, and decision-making rules. Have all incorporators execute the articles by signing and affixing personal seals, then have the articles notarized by a Korean notary public. Foreign incorporators must submit an apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney. Retain the notarial certificate together with all signed originals for submission to the Registry Office.
required_dossiers: Proposed Korean trade name and second-choice name
Signed draft Articles of Incorporation
Passport or other official identification of each incorporator
Apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney for foreign incorporators
Notarial certificate of execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of a conflict or prohibited sign, select the next approved alternative name, amend the Articles of Incorporation, re-notarize all signing pages, and resubmit the clearance request. No delinquency penalty applies if the correction is made before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Deposit and Escrow Balance Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed under the Banking Act of Korea; for non-resident subscribers, the foreign exchange bank handling the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act report.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital subscription account in the proposed corporate name at a Korean commercial bank before the registration of incorporation. All subscribers must transfer or deposit their respective cash contributions into this blocked account, which may not be withdrawn by the promoters. After all funds are credited, request an official bank certificate of deposit stating subscriber names, contribution amounts, account number, and confirmation that the funds remain on deposit. If any subscriber is a non-resident, file the foreign direct investment report with the bank, obtain the foreign-investment registration certificate, and ensure that remittance records match each subscriber's contribution schedule.
required_dossiers: Full amount of subscribed capital
Remittance or deposit slip for each subscriber
Passport and alien registration card of foreign subscriber, where applicable
Foreign direct investment report form and foreign-investment registration certificate
Bank certificate of deposit for the temporary capital subscription account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays issuance of the balance certificate due to anti-money laundering inquiries, provide enhanced due diligence documents such as source of funds, bank reference, and corporate organizational chart. If a written refusal is issued, escalate to the bank's compliance officer and, if necessary, to the Financial Supervisory Service for inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registry Office with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing through iROS; registration tax collection handled by the court office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the competent District Court Registry Office after all subscriptions have been paid and the notarized Articles of Incorporation are executed. Complete the standardized application form, attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank balance certificate, consent-to-appointment instruments of directors and any statutory auditor, lease or ownership evidence for the registered office, seal registration certificate, and proof of payment of registration tax, education surtax, and court stamp fees. Appoint a licensed legal assistant or attorney with a notarized power of attorney where administrative representation is needed. Receive the certified copy of the commercial register after examination and verification by the registry judge.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
Consent-to-appointment documents for directors and statutory auditor
Lease agreement or evidence of registered office
Company seal registration certificate and personal seal certificates
Receipt of payment of registration tax, education surtax, and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order or suspension notice, cure the stated defects within the statutory two-week challenge period by filing supplementary documents or correcting the application. If the registrar refuses registration, appeal the disposition under the Administrative Litigation Act or request an ex officio review by the Supreme Court Registration Division.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Tax, Banking, and Corporate Governance Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service local district tax office; relevant municipal government; Korean commercial bank for operations; social insurance institutions for workplace staff.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certified commercial register, apply to the local district tax office for a business registration certificate and VAT registration using the certified copy of the commercial register and corporate seal certificate. Open a permanent corporate operating bank account and cause the temporary subscription account to be released for the company's use. File the corporate establishment notification with the National Tax Service and, if employees are engaged, register the workplace with the National Pension, Health Insurance, Employment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation insurance systems. Maintain the statutory ownership register of the Yuhan Hoesa, issue unit certificates to all members, and record transfers and encumbrances in accordance with the Commercial Act. Prepare appropriate board and member resolutions for continued operations and regulatory filings.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the commercial register
Business registration certificate application
Corporate seal certificate
Lease agreement for the operating office
Temporary bank account release documentation
Social insurance workplace establishment forms
Ownership register and unit certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects or delays the business registration certificate, supplement the application with the certified copy of the commercial register, lease contract, and bank account statement; if the social insurance authority queries the workplace, present the employment contracts and office lease evidence. Escalate unresolved issues through the National Tax Service homepage and request a written disposition for administrative appeal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is a pure digital and consulting operation under ISIC 6201 (Computer Programming) and NAICS 511210 providing a Multi-Channel Omni-Helpdesk and Conversational Bot Cloud; it does not operate manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing premises requiring an industrial license from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or municipal industrial authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no factory establishment permit, industrial site license, or manufacturing operating permit under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act is required for an ISIC 6201 cloud helpdesk business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Ministry of Environment and Korea Environmental Corporation have no jurisdiction over a non-physical helpdesk SaaS operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no Full EIA Report, Environmental Registration, or Prior Environmental Review is required because the project is neither an infrastructure project nor a physical industrial facility under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no process wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, combustion stack, noise source, or hazardous waste stream is generated by the operation; only ordinary office waste, electronic waste under the Waste Management Act, and wastewater from office sanitary facilities apply at de minimis municipal utility levels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no factory, warehouse, or assembly facility exists, so no Civil Defense fire safety permit, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace approval is required. The company must, however, comply with ordinary office building fire precaution inspections and general Occupational Safety and Health Act duties for employees working in an office environment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic portal for business registration, electronic tax invoices, filing, and payments; Korea Customs Service (KCS) via the UNIPASS system for export declaration and customs clearance evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: As a Korean Yuhan Hoesa incorporated under the Commercial Act, the entity is a domestic corporation and must register for its 10-digit business registration number, which serves as the unified corporate tax and VAT identification number. The representative director must file the business registration application with the responsible NTS district tax office within 20 days from the commencement of business. Required supporting documents include the articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, commercial registration certificate, lease agreement or title deed evidencing the head-office premises, identification of the representative director, and, if any shareholder is a non-resident, the shareholder corporate certificate and passport of the authorized foreign signatory. Non-resident shareholders may be represented under a power-of-attorney, and no minimum paid-in capital is required under Korean law for the registration itself. Upon completion, NTS issues the business registration number through HomeTax, which is simultaneously recognized for Corporate Tax, Value-Added Tax, and Withholding Tax purposes. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean domestic business establishment that supplies electronic services or digital goods to Korean recipients, the entity must instead complete the mandatory simplified VAT registration under the Value-Added Tax Act through HomeTax; this generates a separate simplified VAT registration number and requires the appointment of a tax representative or statutory tax agent in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax classification is not elective. A Yuhan Hoesa is automatically treated as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level worldwide income taxation under the Corporate Tax Act. There is no check-the-box election, no pass-through treatment analogous to a US LLC, and no domestic hybrid-mismatch election. A group-wide consolidated corporate tax regime exists under the Corporate Tax Act, but it is available only to qualifying domestic corporate groups and is not an elective entity classification mechanism for a standalone LLC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold. Any person, including a domestic corporation or a foreign non-resident entity, that commences taxable supply activity in Korea is mandatorily required to register for VAT. Foreign non-resident suppliers of electronic services or digital content to Korean consumers are separately required to complete simplified VAT registration without any turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Every VAT-registered business in Korea is required to issue an electronic tax invoice for taxable supplies made to other registered businesses. The electronic tax invoice must be created through the HomeTax system and transmitted to NTS, using the statutory OpenAPI or EDI channel, by the day following the date the electronic tax invoice is issued. For certain self-billed electronic tax invoices, including those issued by foreign non-resident simplified VAT registrants, transmission occurs on the statutory due date associated with the VAT return. Korea does not operate a real-time pre-clearance digital stamping or fiscal clearance platform; NTS instead performs near-real-time reconciliation of transmitted electronic tax invoices against VAT returns, and each transmitted electronic invoice receives a digital verification number that evidences NTS receipt and integrity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT treatment is available under the Value-Added Tax Act for goods physically exported from Korea and for services supplied to non-residents or foreign persons where the service is deemed to be consumed or used outside Korea under the statutory place-of-supply rules. For the Helpdesk SaaS cloud business, export zero-rating will apply where the customers are foreign non-residents, the contract is executed from the Korean entity's foreign-facing commercial channel, the assistance and software platform are delivered from cloud infrastructure located outside Korea or used exclusively outside Korea, and the consideration is received in foreign currency. The supplier must demonstrate that the recipient is a non-resident and that the service is not actually consumed in Korea. Services supplied from Korea to Korean residents or performed in Korea for a foreign counterparty do not qualify for zero-rating unless a specific statutory exception applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Certificate issued by Korea Customs Service through the UNIPASS system for physical goods, evidencing the exportation of goods and matching the commercial invoice
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing shipment of the goods from Korea to the foreign destination
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, Purchase Order, and executed international sales contract showing the foreign non-resident counterparty
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency

For digital helpdesk and SaaS services: service contract with declared non-resident customer, customer identity and registration documents, cloud service usage logs and server location records, IP access evidence, and detailed billing and payment settlement records demonstrating offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS can challenge an export zero-rating claim in VAT audits and may require production of all supporting export and foreign-exchange documentation for each zero-rated transaction. If the documentation is missing, false, or inconsistent, NTS will reclassify the supply as domestic taxable at the 10% standard VAT rate, assess the unpaid VAT, impose penalty surcharges under the Value-Added Tax Act for underreporting, false tax invoices, and negligent non-payment, and add late-payment interest at the statutory rate of 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount. When zero-rated input VAT refunds were previously paid, NTS will issue a reassessment and clawback the refund with these surcharges and interest. In cases of deliberate concealment, forgery, or fraudulent export or remittance documentation, the matter can be referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exposing responsible persons to imprisonment and criminal fines in addition to the civil tax liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the foreign-exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates an open current account regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; KRW is convertible for genuine trade and service payments, but all cross-border transactions are monitored through foreign exchange banks. Current account receipts such as SaaS export proceeds may be collected in foreign currency or KRW, but service exporters must collect proceeds within 180 days. There is no surrender obligation and no fixed mandatory conversion ratio; exporters may maintain foreign currency proceeds in designated foreign exchange accounts until used for working capital. Capital account transactions are subject to a negative-list system. Inward foreign investment into Yuhan Hoesa must be notified under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and paid-in capital must be routed through a Korean foreign-exchange bank escrow account before capital verification. Profit repatriation is possible as dividends after audited financial statements, tax clearance, and showing foreign investment registration; remittances for royalties or service fees require underlying contracts and invoice evidence. In practice, banks treat profit remittance from a low-risk helpdesk SaaS entity as standard but will block or defer if the beneficial owner chain is incomplete, tax residency mismatches arise, or the payment purpose code is inconsistent with supporting documents.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds, including SaaS and helpdesk service receipts, must be collected through a Korean foreign exchange bank within 180 days from the date of service completion or invoice date; a delayed collection report or regulatory approval is required beyond 180 days. Mandatory conversion ratio: none. The exporter may retain proceeds in a foreign-currency account or convert to KRW at its discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for foreign direct investment
Basic Operational KRW and Foreign Currency Account
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account for export proceeds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, and Payoneer are not licensed foreign exchange banks under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and cannot validly receive Korean export proceeds or act as settlement intermediaries for regulated trade payments. Using an EMI for the primary treasury account creates an unresolved foreign exchange reporting event and can trigger AML refusal during corporate account opening. Such EMIs are acceptable only as front-end merchant collection gates, as with Stripe_Billing and PayPal, before funds are automatically swept to a licensed tier-1 Korean bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean tier-1 banks generally require physical presence of at least one statutory director or appointed corporate signatory at the branch during the initial KYC interview. Remote opening may be considered for a low-risk entity when identity verification is performed by secure video call with apostilled corporate documents and certified passport copies, but for a foreign-invested capital account and a foreign exchange settlement account, an in-branch visit is the dominant market standard. A consular proxy opening is not uniformly accepted; local banks prefer a notarized power of attorney, passport-level proof, and a Korean-resident bank officer to verify the underlying business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by foreign shareholders of Yuhan Hoesa and any indirect ownership through an offshore holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extracts for every entity in the ownership chain, apostilled and translated into Korean/English, beneficial ownership declaration forms, passport copies of all natural persons holding a 25% or more interest, and a notarized organizational chart with share percentages and source-of-funds explanation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume digital receipts from Stripe/PayPal flagged as unexplained money mule or third-party payout pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement reports and payout history for 12 months, a bank statement from the merchant acquiring account, invoices and customer contracts linked to each material receivable, helpdesk subscriber dashboard log, and a customer due-diligence policy showing no sanctioned jurisdiction exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Profit remittance or intercompany service fee payment identified as disguised dividend repatriation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer pricing master file and local file under Korean transfer pricing rules, benchmarked intercompany agreements, annual time-sheet evidence if the helpdesk cloud services are intra-group, a board resolution approving the payment, and a valid Foreign Investment Registration record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance or shell indicator when registered office and directors are outside Korea
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed office lease in Korea, payroll and employment records of Korean staff, VAT filings, tax invoices, corporate bank statements, annual financial statements, and evidence of actual business activities such as cloud SaaS server utilization and customer support operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's bank to Yuhan Hoesa's capital escrow account at a designated Korean foreign-exchange bank. The remittance instruction must reference the Foreign Investment Notification number and the statutory purpose code for inward direct investment in the payment narrative. The receiving bank reports the transaction in the Foreign Exchange Information System and issues the foreign-invested company registration. Funds must remain in the escrow account until capital verification and share issuance; conversion to KRW uses the bank's interbank exchange rate and must not be split into multiple small transfers to avoid structuring flags.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 is the standard rail for service trade settlements; commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not suited to helpdesk SaaS. For disbursements, Yuhan Hoesa should present a service import contract, tax invoice, and foreign exchange recording to the bank. International vendor payments such as cloud infrastructure can be settled through MT103 with the appropriate purpose code, while payments to non-resident directors or related parties require additional underlying agreements and withholding tax clearance. Domestic KRW operating payments are cleared through the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute wire system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore KRW/USD forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank, limited to the notional value of documented export receivables or import payables
Cross-currency swaps used exclusively to hedge identifiable foreign-currency receivables or payables arising from the SaaS helpdesk business; speculative or uncovered swap positions are prohibited

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts are permissible only if structured through an authorized Korean foreign-exchange dealer for genuine economic exposure with underlying documentary support; standalone NDF speculation is not permissible under the Korean legal framework

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December: on or before 31 March of the following year; automatic one-month extension to 30 April if the return is prepared and signed by a licensed tax accountant (세무사)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax; understatement penalty of 10% of the misreported amount; overdue interest accrues at 0.03% per day on unpaid tax; persistent non-filing for six consecutive fiscal years can lead to administrative strike-off from the commercial registry on court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax on Corporate Tax (법인 지방소득세)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si/Gun/Gu) through the Local Tax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as corporate income tax: due on or before 31 March (or 30 April if extended filing is permitted) for fiscal year ending 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 0.75% per month on arrears; 20% penalty on unpaid tax after a demand; continued delinquency may trigger asset seizure and a request for dormant-company strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and approval of financial statements (정기 총회 및 재무제표 승인)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ (minutes recorded in the statutory minute book; no government filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end, i.e., on or before 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting does not carry a direct administrative fine, but directors or managing members may become personally liable for resulting losses and the company cannot lawfully approve the financial statements or audit appointment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Financial Statements filing (외부감사보고서 제출)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the annual general meeting, and in no event later than 15 July if the meeting is held on the statutory last permissible date of 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers an administrative fine of up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 37,000); continued non-compliance can lead to criminal penalties under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and disqualification of directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Invested Enterprise Status Report (외국인투자기업 연차보고)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) filed through the relevant foreign currency bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end, i.e., on or before 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 3 million (approximately USD 2,200) for failure to file; may also result in adverse treatment under foreign-investment incentive regimes

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if (i) it is a listed company; (ii) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year exceed KRW 120 billion (approximately USD 89 million); (iii) total assets exceed KRW 70 billion (approximately USD 52 million) and total liabilities also exceed KRW 70 billion; (iv) annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion (approximately USD 74 million); (v) the entity is a financial company, public-interest legal entity, or issuer of securities to the public; or (vi) the company is otherwise designated by the Financial Services Commission under scale tests based on balance sheet size, turnover, and number of employees (generally more than 300 regular employees) as stipulated by Presidential Decree. The audit must be performed by a CPA firm or a registered external auditor under Article 3 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for externally audited companies; non-public companies not mandatorily audited may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP); small and medium enterprises may use the SME Accounting Standards under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the Korean Accounting Standards Board rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Korean law, a Yuhan Hoesa must maintain an up-to-date register of members (사원명부). Any transfer of equity, change in members' names, addresses, or capital contributions must be filed with the competent district court registry within four weeks (approximately 30 days) of the occurrence. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation filing for ordinary closed companies; however, foreign-invested companies are required to submit an annual foreign-investment status report to MOTIE by 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year. Additionally, financial institutions are obliged to identify and verify the ultimate beneficial owner for FATF compliance, and any change in beneficial ownership exceeding a 10% threshold must be reported to the relevant financial institution without delay.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 500 - 1,500 USD (outsourced registered office or corporate agent annual fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000 - 25,000 USD depending on entity size, cross-border revenue, and IFRS conversion requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.2% (aggregated national corporate income tax 22% + local income tax surtax 2.2%) for taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion; progressive lower brackets: 11% on income up to KRW 200 million and 22% on income between KRW 200 million and KRW 30 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean Special Tax Treatment Control Act (STTCL) offers R&D tax credits of up to 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure for software/cloud businesses; small and medium enterprises (SME) benefit from reduced rates and cash-accounting (cash basis) options for revenue recognition; foreign-invested companies in certain high-tech or digital service projects may receive a 50% corporate tax reduction for 5 years; no separate patent box is available but income from user-developed software may qualify for R&D deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return Form (Bupin Ployn Tax Pyo, Form No. 12-2, plus attached schedules) filed via the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic portal at hometax.go.kr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; semi-annual interim prepayment returns are also due for corporations (August 31 and March 31 for a calendar-year entity)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for a calendar-year company); automatic one-month extension to April 30 if the financial statements are audited by an independent external auditor; further extension of up to 2 months may be granted for foreign-invested companies subject to foreign audit rules or upon showing just cause

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: legal name, corporate registration number, address, business classification (ISIC code), and fiscal-year date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the ultimate non-resident beneficial shareholders, including name, country of tax residence, Tax Residency Certificate number, ownership percentage, and any double-tax treaty positioning; failure to provide complete non-resident particulars may trigger withholding tax penalties and denial of treaty relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue: aggregated global receipts from all helpdesk, customer-support SaaS subscriptions, and cloud chatbot services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When non-resident payments enter through Stripe/PayPal, convert all foreign-currency revenue into KRW using the Bank of Korea base exchange rate for the transaction date or the last day of the month; do not omit revenue booked to offshore payment facilitators; all revenue is taxable in Korea because the entity is a Korean domestic corporation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: report gross income after deductible business expenses, depreciation, amortization, and net operating loss carryovers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible cross-border payments (e.g., management fees or royalties paid to offshore related parties that lack economic substance) and any expenses not properly evidenced; adjust for permanent and temporary differences; specifically, expenses paid to non-resident related parties are deductible only if supported by arm's-length documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income and foreign tax credit: report any Korean-source and foreign-source income and attach foreign tax credit computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Since Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean resident entity, worldwide income is taxable; if the entity receives dividends or royalty income from foreign subsidiaries, claim a foreign tax credit for withholding taxes paid abroad; maintain supporting documents including overseas tax assessment notices; uncredited foreign taxes may be deducted as an expense in accordance with the Korean Corporate Tax Act

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident shareholder dividend withholding tax computation: on declared or deemed dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate statutory withholding on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders at 20% national corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax surtax (total 22%) unless a reduced treaty rate applies; attach the relevant treaty relief form and the non-resident's Tax Residency Certificate before applying the reduced rate; under-withholding here exposes the company to full statutory tax, interest, and penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Intercompany and transfer pricing disclosures: details of cross-border related-party transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all transactions with non-resident related parties: customer support subcontracting fees, intercompany software licensing, support fees, and interest on intercompany loans; disclose the arm's-length methodology used, produce a Local File if the aggregate cross-border related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 50 billion, and state whether a Master File and Country-by-Country report are required; non-disclosure will trigger separate documentation penalties and possible tax adjustments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing of the Corporate Income Tax Return triggers a negligence penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid tax if the return is not filed on time, and an additional 10% negligence penalty for underreported tax; unpaid tax after the due date accrues a daily delinquency surcharge (approximately 0.0225% per day); fraudulent or evasive filing is a criminal offense under the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act, carrying imprisonment of up to 2 years or a fine of up to 200% of the evaded tax; directors may also be designated as a 'secondary liable person' and subject to travel restrictions (blacklisting) until tax arrears are settled

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wHT_rate: 22% (20% national corporate income tax + 2% local income tax surtax) on outbound dividends paid to non-resident shareholders under domestic law; reduced to 15% (or 10% for shareholdings above 25%) under the Korea-OECD Model Tax Treaty where 5% or 15% treaty rates apply based on the shareholding threshold; if no treaty claim, the full 22% is withheld
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Tax Agreement (DTA) reduced rate, the non-resident shareholder must submit: (i) a completed 'Application for Income Tax Exemption or Reduction under a Tax Treaty' to the Korean withholding agent (payor) before payment; (ii) the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority confirming residence in the treaty jurisdiction and valid for the relevant fiscal year; (iii) a beneficial ownership declaration identifying the ultimate recipients and confirming that the dividends are not streamed through a conduit; and (iv) supporting substance documentation (e.g., board resolutions, account statements) to show the recipient has economic capacity to hold shares; the Korean payor must report these documents to the NTS through the HomeTax system; if reduced treaty relief is requested after the withholding has been made, the non-resident may file a refund claim with the NTS within three years from the statutory filing deadline of the withholding officer; failure to submit the TRC and beneficial ownership evidence before or at the time of payment will force withholding at the statutory 22% rate with no retroactive relief
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest paid to non-residents is also 22% (20% + 2% local surtax); Korea's tax treaties typically reduce interest to 10%, and royalties to 10% or 15% depending on the treaty; treaty relief is available only if the recipient is the beneficial owner and provides the TRC and the same procedural application form as for dividends; for royalties related to the use of software, cloud-based customer helpdesk technology, patents, or know-how, the Korean payer must obtain a Foreign Exchange/Cross-Border Transaction Certificate and submit the withholding return and payment through HomeTax within 10 days of the payment; interest on intercompany loans must satisfy the arm's-length interest rate test and the Korean thin capitalization rule (debt:equity ratio 2:1 for general businesses; 5:1 for financial institutions) to avoid reclassification of interest as constructive dividends

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File and Master File are mandatory when the aggregate cross-border related-party transaction amount for the fiscal year exceeds KRW 50 billion (approximately USD 38 million); Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting is required if the multinational group's consolidated revenue is at least KRW 1 trillion (approximately USD 750 million) with operating revenue from foreign subsidiaries above KRW 100 billion; even below these thresholds, transactional records and arm's-length documentation must be maintained contemporaneously
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Korea does not apply BVI-style Economic Substance Regulations, the Korean tax authorities apply the 'substance over form' doctrine under the Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 14, and the Corporate Tax Act Art. 20/21 rules against sham transactions; a Korean company must carry on its business with actual employees, office premises, management and operational risk in Korea to be recognized as the beneficial owner of income and to be eligible for treaty benefits; Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) for a helpdesk SaaS provider include the development and maintenance of the software platform, contracting with customers, risk management, billing and support functions, which must be performed in Korea if the entity is the contract party; reliance solely on offshore subcontractors with no Korean substance will trigger re-characterization of revenue, denial of treaty benefits, and be treated as a shell company under the OECD/G20 BEPS MLI

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Omitted or Falsified Digital Service Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company deliberately under-reports customer-support SaaS subscription revenue or receives subscription fees directly into personal or offshore Stripe/PayPal accounts without remitting funds to the Korean corporate bank account and without declaring the revenue to the NTS, or issues forged invoice documents to hide the true taxable income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act, Art. 3, evading corporate tax by fraud or other unlawful means is penalized with imprisonment for up to 2 years or a criminal fine not less than 50% but not exceeding 200% of the amount of evaded tax; in addition, the NTS imposes a 20% negligence penalty on the omitted tax amount plus daily delinquency surcharges; if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, the criminal penalty is aggravated to imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine up to 300% of the evaded amount
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: the responsible director is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and interest; the NTS can attach director's personal bank accounts, real estate and equity holdings; the director will be placed on the national tax delinquent list, resulting in a travel ban (blacklisting) and restrictions on receiving government licenses; upon criminal conviction, the director faces actual imprisonment without probation, confiscation of profits, and disqualification from serving as a director of any Korean entity for up to 10 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Profit Shifting to Offshore Affiliates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company enters into artificial intercompany arrangements with Hong Kong, Singapore, or Delaware affiliates, charging excessively high royalty, support, or subcontracting fees for low-value helpdesk services that shift profits out of Korea; the arrangement lacks commercial rationality and no actual service is performed by the offshore recipient; the company also fails to prepare and submit the Local File, Master File or CbC report despite exceeding statutory thresholds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Korean Corporate Tax Act Art. 20 and Art. 21, the NTS is authorized to re-determine taxable income by applying the arm's-length principle and may impose an underreporting negligence penalty of up to 20% of the adjusted underreported tax, plus 10% for unsubstantiated international transaction disclosures; where a CbC report is required but not filed, the penalty is KRW 50 million for the first non-compliance and KRW 200 million for repeated non-compliance; tax adjustments may also trigger a 60% fraud penalty for intentional manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorized or signed the manipulated transfer-pricing documentation are personally liable for the additional corporate tax, interest and penalties discovered on audit; the NTS may seek indemnity from the director's personal assets; in serious cases, the act is deemed tax evasion and subject to the same criminal imprisonment terms as under the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act; directors may also be debarred from holding office in any company that transacts with Korean financial institutions, and the government may impose an exit ban for pending cross-border tax disputes

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Substance and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity is established as a naked shell with no office, no employees, no decision-making authority, and no actual business activity in Korea; it is used solely to hold invoices and divert profits to a low-tax jurisdiction, or it claims treaty benefits on outbound payments without carrying on genuine economic activities; the company falsely declares itself as a beneficial owner of the revenue while all customer support and development is actually carried out by related foreign entities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 14, transactions that are a sham or mere form are disregarded for tax purposes, resulting in full assessment of the hidden profits to the Korean entity; the Council for International Tax Coordination Act (CITCA) and the Korean Multilateral Instrument (MLI) ratification allow the NTS to deny treaty benefits if the main purpose of the arrangement is to obtain treaty relief; a 40%-60% additional penalty may be imposed on abusive tax avoidance transactions; in extreme cases, the criminal anti-tax-evasion penalties described above apply
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the full amount of tax, penalties, and interest if the corporate veil is pierced; courts have historically pierced the veil for gross undercapitalization and absence of separate control; directors face civil liability for asset restitution, loss of limited liability protection, immediate travel restriction order until the tax liability is settled, and criminal conviction for conspiracy to commit tax fraud with imprisonment up to 5 years and a personal criminal fine equal to 300% of the evaded tax; the director's personal passport can be invalidated and the director placed on the Interpol red notice if the liability exceeds KRW 300 million
